newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tenaga plans 18.0 bln rgt power spending.
newsitem.headline: Tenaga plans 18.0 bln rgt power spending.

text.p: Malaysian utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd plans to spend 18.0 billion ringgit on electricity infrastructure between now and the year 2002, according to company executive chairman Ahmad Tajuddin Ali.

"We aim to invest by the year 2002, a total of 18.0 billion ringgit to help ensure that we can meet the projected future energy needs of Malaysia," Tajuddin said in a report accompanying the company's just-released annual report.

In his first official statements to shareholders since taking over Tenaga's leadership on September 1, Tajuddin said the company plans to spend 6.0 billion ringgit to strengthen its power supply system in the next five years.
Tajuddin replaced Ani Arope as head of the state-run utility after a blackout engulfed peninsula Malaysia on August 3 for 12-15 hours. It was the second major power outage in four years.
Tajuddin said the utility is improving the design of the protective system "with the hope that a major power interruption will never happen again".
